hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{2\sin(\pi x-3\pi)-4}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one).

hints.content:
The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin(\pi x)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $\pi$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\pi}=0.5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin(\pi x)}$ to $\red{2\sin(\pi x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $2$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one half, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one half, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one half, two).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{2\sin(\pi x)}$ to $\blue{2\sin(\pi x-3\pi)-4}$, which is equivalent to $2\sin{\large(}\pi(x-3){\large)}-4$, is a translation to the right by $3$ units and a translation downwards by $4$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(3,-4\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(3.5,-2)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (three, negative four) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three and one half, negative two).

question.content:
**Graph $h(x)=2\sin(\pi x-3\pi)-4$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
